text:
ravi: quick note from Athena9b onboarding (gguf -> int8): generation looks fine until ~1k tokens then outputs jump to garbage when tokenizer.pad_token_id != 0.
jen: hmm, is that reproduced on fp16? or only after quantization+packing?
omar: only on int8 artifacts so far. fp16 export behaves. repro attached.
ravi: minimal repro pasted: 
```
# tokens around pad boundary
input_ids = [11, 22, 333, 1023, 5, 5, 5]  # pad_token_id=5
config = {"use_cache": True, "max_new_tokens": 64}
# run and inspect kv index map + head offsets
```
jen: could be head packing/layout mismatch between converter and runtime (we saw similar with head_map permutations before). Did exporter include any metadata?
omar: gguf metadata contains "head_permutation" with non-canonical ordering. converter left permutation in file; runtime expects contiguous head-major layout. when packer computes kv pointers it ends up pointing into pad area for some heads.
ravi: confirmed: kv_offsets show heads 0..7 aligned, 8..15 shifted by half-head stride. result: half heads read wrong slices and combined with pad offsets produces garbage.
jen: short-term: loader can apply head_permutation at load to canonicalize (memory copy ~10% cold start). long-term: converter should rewrite weights into canonical order.
omar: agree. I'll add a quick detector in onboarding: if gguf contains head_permutation -> fail and suggest converter flag or auto-reorder. also add pad-sweep smoke (pad_id 0..12) across long contexts.
loader-bot: onboarding job queued: athena9b-int8-pad-sweep (job id 7654).
ravi: uploaded a tiny failing slice to s3://redwood-onboard/athena9b/1765432199/kv-sample.tar.gz and filed ticket with steps.
jen: please add a unit test in runtime packer to ensure pad_token_id invariance for kv indexing. that would have caught it earlier.
omar: will add integ test and open PR in model-converters to emit canonical-ordered gguf by default. will also document loader flag to auto-reorder for expediency.
ravi: thanks team. leaving notes on the ticket and will follow up with perf numbers for loader-relayout. :thumbsup:
